title: Florida National Guard Deploys Emergency Response to Kentucky Ice Storms
description: Package about Fla. National Guard deploying regional emergency response networks for the Ky. ice storms. Produced by Lt. Col. Ron Tittle.
keywords: 290th Combat Comm Support Sqadron, J-6 Infromation Management, Chief Warrant Officer Michael Jordan, Jacksonville
unit_name: Florida National Guard Public Affairs Office
credit: Lt. Col. Ron Tittle, Lt Col (Ret)

transcript.text: This is an FLNG News Break for Saturday, January 31st, 2009.
The Florida National Guard sent some of its regional emergency response networks
or RERNs today to aid Kentucky heavily impacted by ice storms.
Well, we've been called upon to assist Kentucky with this ice storm that they had.
They've lost a lot of their communications assets, so we're going to take these emergency systems
that we have here in Florida and provide them with emergency communications.
Florida's Information Management Specialist worked through the night at the Camp Blending Joint Training Center,
south of Jacksonville, to prepare the mobile communications equipment used to enhance communications,
such as phones, internet connection, computers, and interagency radio connections.
We've already packed up three and already got them on trucks to ship them out,
and we're finishing up with three additional systems.
Numerous trailer mounted RERNs were set up quickly, turned on, checked and were loaded on commercial transporters.
Some of the Guard members were already sent to Kentucky to receive the RERNs.
We'll be operated by the Florida Air National Guard's 2-9th Joint Communication Support Squadron,
headquarter DAG-MEG-DIL Air Force Base.
The operating teams were called up and were already enrout to Kentucky.
We'll be more of a... they'll set up the systems and the operators will actually provide assistance
to extend networks, provide things like laptops, IP phones.
The RERNs and their operators will be in Kentucky as long as they are needed.
They're in this winter.
We'll bring them back through.
We'll inventory them, clean everything up.
We'll do an inspection to make sure everything's still working properly for the next mission.
Reporting for Florida National Guard Public Affairs, I'm Lieutenant Colonel Ron Tittle.
